title: Deterministic replay for mixed-quantization kernels and heterogeneous GPU occupancy during multi-stream decode
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Intermittent non-deterministic CUDA Graph captures and replay failures observed in mixed-quantization model variants (int8 + fp16 kernels) when multi-stream decode runs at varying occupancy levels. Symptoms include graph recapture mismatches across streams, sporadic assertion failures in kernel args validation during replay, and degraded tail-latency as streams fall back to per-call execution. This ticket scopes the diagnostic, fix and validation work to make capture/replay deterministic across mixed kernel codepaths and heterogeneous occupancy profiles.
background: We started seeing a reproduction signal after rolling quantized int8 kernels for several decoder attention blocks. At low occupancy, the kernel-selector picks an int8 fused attention kernel, while under higher occupancy it favors an fp16 tiled attention kernel for thermal/perf reasons. Because these choices affect recorded kernel argument layouts, CUDA Graph recapture produced different graph node sequences for concurrent streams. Existing capture normalization logic assumes kernel selection is stable during a capture window; that assumption breaks with mixed-quant variants and co-resident workloads on the same GPU. Past tickets addressed related capture fencing and kernel arbitration but did not cover quantization-induced layout differences.
proposed_solution: 1) Build a kernel compatibility matrix keyed by (model-arch, layer, quantization-profile, occupancy-hint) so that kernel selector returns a canonical 'capture-category' for a given request. 2) Normalize capture seeds by injecting a lightweight capture-seed header into graph metadata so replay compares categories rather than raw kernel pointers. 3) Add an occupancy-aware kernel binder that pins kernel variants to capture-categories during the prefill phase (before graph begin). 4) Introduce an atomic prefill fence that serializes capture-critical path for the first N prefill tokens when a mixed-quantization profile is detected. 5) Expand the replay validation harness to run randomized mixed-occupancy fuzz (CI) and a deterministic smoke test (nightly) across representative hardware profiles.
acceptance_criteria: No graph recapture mismatches for mixed-quantization decoder jobs in the harbor test cluster for 2000 randomized seeds
Reproduction rate of previous assertion failures drops to 0 in CI and staging over a 7-day window
Tail p95/p99 decode latency in production remains within 5% of baseline for representative workloads after rollout
Kernel selector exposes a stable capture-category API consumed by capture/replay logic
Integration tests added to CI that exercise occupancy transitions mid-capture and validate identical graph metadata across streams
tasks: Instrument kernel selector to emit capture-category (ENG change)
Implement compatibility matrix and populate from model onboarding data
Add prefill atomic fence and occupancy-hint checks in capture runtime
Modify graph metadata to include capture-seed and category tags
Extend replay validator: fuzz harness + deterministic suite
End-to-end staging run and collection of flaky capture traces
Rollout plan and gradual ramp with kill-switch metrics
tests: Unit tests for kernel selector -> category mapping with mixed-quant fixtures
Harness: spawn 8 streams with randomized occupancy changes and validate graph metadata equality
Nightly matrix: combinations of (int8,int4,fp16) x (low,medium,high occupancy) on T4/A10/A100
Canary in production with verbose capture-compare logging for first 24 hours
rollout_plan: Feature-gate the occupancy-aware binder behind runtime flag runtime.capture.stable_mixed_quant. Start with canary on 2 GPU hosts (staging) for 48h, then expand to 10% of production traffic for 72h while monitoring graph_mismatch_count and tail latency; abort if graph_mismatch_count > 0 or p99 latency regression > 10%. If stable, ramp to 100% over 3 days. Provide on-call runbook to disable flag and revert metadata schema if required.
